description: CDK infrastructure for the async path: the worker + submit Lambdas, the two new API Gateway v2 routes (POST /jobs, GET /jobs/{id}), the exact per-role least-privilege IAM statements, and DynamoDB TTL on the MovieIntel table, all locked by extended synth assertions. Depends on FEAT-002 (the handler packages handlers.submit / handlers.worker must exist so the asset ships them and the handler strings resolve). Touches infra/serving_stack.py, infra/pipeline_stack.py, and the two infra synth test files.
steps: infra/pipeline_stack.py _dynamodb_table(): add `time_to_live_attribute="expires_at"` to the existing dynamodb.Table(self, 'MovieIntelTable', ...) constructor call (design Decision 2 — co-located with the table definition; backward-compatible, existing items without expires_at never expire).

tests/infra/test_pipeline_stack_synth.py: add one assertion that the AWS::DynamoDB::Table resource has TimeToLiveSpecification == {'AttributeName': 'expires_at', 'Enabled': True} (via template.has_resource_properties or by reading find_resources). Keep the existing table assertions intact.

infra/serving_stack.py: add self.worker_function (lambda_.Function 'WorkerFn', runtime PYTHON_3_12, handler 'handlers.worker.handler.handler', code from INFRA_DIR with HANDLER_ASSET_EXCLUDES, layers=[self.shared_layer] (NO _sqlite layer), environment=self._environment() (full serving env), timeout=Duration.minutes(5), memory_size=1024) and self.submit_function (lambda_.Function 'SubmitFn', handler 'handlers.submit.handler.handler', same asset+shared layer, timeout=Duration.seconds(10), memory_size=256). Create the worker FIRST, then set submit env: self.submit_function.add_environment('WORKER_FUNCTION_NAME', self.worker_function.function_name), and add MOVIEINTEL_TABLE_NAME / MOVIEINTEL_GSI1_NAME (reuse the table/gsi values from self.persistence). Build these in __init__ after self.serving_function.

infra/serving_stack.py: add a `_grant_async_iam()` method and call it from __init__ after both async functions exist (keep `_grant_iam()` for ServingFn unchanged). Implement the EXACT statements from design 'IAM': SubmitFn S1 = PolicyStatement(actions=['dynamodb:PutItem','dynamodb:UpdateItem','dynamodb:GetItem'], resources=[table_arn]) (base table ARN ONLY — NO GSI1, NO Query/Scan/BatchGetItem); SubmitFn S2 = self.worker_function.grant_invoke(self.submit_function). WorkerFn W1 = bedrock:InvokeModel on bedrock_invoke_model_resources(region, account); W2 = bedrock:ApplyGuardrail on self.guardrail.attr_guardrail_arn; W3 = bedrock:Retrieve on arn:aws:bedrock:{region}:{account}:knowledge-base/YNXUIXEYBQ (reuse DEPLOYED_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ID); W4 = ['dynamodb:GetItem','dynamodb:BatchGetItem','dynamodb:Query','dynamodb:Scan'] on [table_arn, index_arn]; W5 = ['dynamodb:PutItem','dynamodb:UpdateItem','dynamodb:GetItem'] on [table_arn]. No bedrock:* and no Resource '*' anywhere.

infra/serving_stack.py _http_api(): add a new HttpLambdaIntegration('SubmitIntegration', handler=self.submit_function) and add_routes for path '/jobs' methods=[POST] and path '/jobs/{id}' methods=[GET] on self.api, both using the submit integration (CORS/WAF inherit at the API level — no change). Add an informational CfnOutput for the submit route in _outputs(); keep ServingApiUrl unchanged. Note the handler reads the {id} path variable from event['pathParameters']['id'] (FEAT-002), so the route template is '/jobs/{id}'.

tests/infra/test_serving_stack_synth.py: update the module to the new reality — THREE python3.12 Lambdas and FOUR routes. Fix test_single_serving_lambda_with_handler_string (now also assert the submit+worker handlers exist, or scope it to find the serve handler among three), fix the route-count/route-keys assertion in test_api_gateway_integrated_with_the_lambda (resource_count_is for AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Route becomes 4 and route_keys == {'POST /query','GET /health','POST /jobs','GET /jobs/{id}'}), and fix test_serving_dynamodb_is_read_only so it scopes the read-only check to the ServingFn role (the submit/worker roles legitimately hold write actions now) — identify the ServingFn policy by its bedrock:Retrieve+table read fingerprint, or restructure to assert per-role.

tests/infra/test_serving_stack_synth.py: ADD the design-mandated assertions — (a) two new AWS::Lambda::Function with Handler 'handlers.submit.handler.handler' (Timeout 10, MemorySize 256) and 'handlers.worker.handler.handler' (Timeout 300, MemorySize 1024), neither Layers including a _sqlite layer and both including the shared layer; (b) two new AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Route with RouteKey 'POST /jobs' and 'GET /jobs/{id}' integrated to the submit integration, existing POST /query + GET /health retained; (c) the SubmitFn role policy contains dynamodb PutItem/UpdateItem/GetItem scoped to the table ARN with NO GSI1 resource and NO Query/Scan/BatchGetItem/bedrock:* action, plus lambda:InvokeFunction scoped to the worker function; (d) the WorkerFn role policy contains bedrock:InvokeModel, bedrock:ApplyGuardrail, bedrock:Retrieve, the DynamoDB tool-read actions on table+GSI1, and the DynamoDB job-write actions on the table, with NO Resource '*' and NO bedrock:* wildcard. Match ARNs on stringified statements (account id is a synth token) as the existing tests do.
acceptance_criteria: `cd infra && npx aws-cdk@2 synth MovieIntelServingStack` succeeds (AC-14) and `cd infra && npx aws-cdk@2 synth MovieIntelPipelineStack` succeeds.
`uv run pytest tests/infra/test_serving_stack_synth.py tests/infra/test_pipeline_stack_synth.py` passes, including the new submit/worker function, two-route, per-role IAM, and TTL assertions.
No IAM statement uses bedrock:* or Resource '*'; SubmitFn has no GSI1/Query/Scan/Bedrock grant; the TTL attribute is expires_at and Enabled.
`uv run mypy src` and a local `uv run mypy` (covering infra) pass; `uv run ruff check .` passes.
verification: cd infra && npx aws-cdk@2 synth MovieIntelServingStack
cd infra && npx aws-cdk@2 synth MovieIntelPipelineStack
uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy src
findings: DONE. Four files changed. (1) infra/pipeline_stack.py _dynamodb_table(): added time_to_live_attribute='expires_at' to the dynamodb.Table('MovieIntelTable', ...) call (backward compatible; movie items without expires_at never expire). (2) tests/infra/test_pipeline_stack_synth.py: added test_table_has_ttl_on_expires_at asserting TimeToLiveSpecification=={'AttributeName':'expires_at','Enabled':True} via has_resource_properties; existing table assertions intact. (3) infra/serving_stack.py: added self.worker_function (_worker_lambda: 'WorkerFn', PYTHON_3_12, handler 'handlers.worker.handler.handler', INFRA_DIR asset + HANDLER_ASSET_EXCLUDES, layers=[shared_layer], environment=_environment() full serving env, timeout 5min, memory 1024) created BEFORE self.submit_function (_submit_lambda: 'SubmitFn', handler 'handlers.submit.handler.handler', same asset+shared layer, env MOVIEINTEL_TABLE_NAME/MOVIEINTEL_GSI1_NAME + WORKER_FUNCTION_NAME=worker.function_name via add_environment, timeout 10s, memory 256); both built in __init__ after serving_function + _grant_iam(). Added _grant_async_iam() called after both async fns exist (ServingFn _grant_iam unchanged): SubmitFn S1=PutItem/UpdateItem/GetItem on table_arn ONLY (no GSI1, no Query/Scan/BatchGetItem), S2=worker.grant_invoke(submit); WorkerFn W1=bedrock:InvokeModel on bedrock_invoke_model_resources(region,account), W2=bedrock:ApplyGuardrail on guardrail.attr_guardrail_arn, W3=bedrock:Retrieve on knowledge-base/YNXUIXEYBQ (DEPLOYED_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ID), W4=GetItem/BatchGetItem/Query/Scan on [table_arn,index_arn], W5=PutItem/UpdateItem/GetItem on [table_arn]. No bedrock:* and no Resource '*'. _http_api() adds HttpLambdaIntegration('SubmitIntegration', handler=submit_function) and two add_routes: path '/jobs' POST and path '/jobs/{id}' GET (constants JOBS_ROUTE_PATH='/jobs', JOB_POLL_ROUTE_PATH='/jobs/{id}'); CORS/WAF inherit at API level. Added informational CfnOutput 'ServingSubmitUrl'; ServingApiUrl unchanged. (4) tests/infra/test_serving_stack_synth.py: renamed single-lambda test to test_three_lambdas_with_expected_handler_strings (asserts the 3 handler strings); scoped env-pins test and read-only DynamoDB test to the ServingFn (identified by bedrock:Retrieve + read-only DynamoDB fingerprint); route-count/keys now 4 == {POST /query, GET /health, POST /jobs, GET /jobs/{id}}; ApplyGuardrail statement count now 2 (ServingFn + WorkerFn), both token resources. Added test_submit_and_worker_function_sizing_and_layers (WorkerFn 300/1024, SubmitFn 10/256, both shared layer, no sqlite layer -- stack has exactly one layer), test_jobs_routes_present_integrated_to_submit (two job routes share the submit integration, distinct from the serve integration), test_submit_role_scoped_to_job_item_and_worker_invoke (S1/S2: no GSI1, no Query/Scan/BatchGetItem/bedrock, lambda:InvokeFunction scoped), test_worker_role_has_bedrock_kb_dynamo_read_and_job_writes (W1-W5 actions, KB+table+GSI1 resources, no Resource '*' / no bedrock:*). VERIFICATION all pass: uv run pytest tests/infra/test_serving_stack_synth.py tests/infra/test_pipeline_stack_synth.py = 35 passed; cd infra && npx aws-cdk@2 synth MovieIntelServingStack and ... MovieIntelPipelineStack both exit 0 (local bundling, no Docker; TTL spec present in pipeline template); uv run ruff check . + ruff format --check . clean; uv run mypy src = ok, local uv run mypy (covers infra) = ok (147 files). NOTE: npx aws-cdk@2 first-run prompts to install the CLI interactively; pre-install with `npx --yes aws-cdk@2 --version` (or pass --yes) before synth or it blocks. The _sqlite-absent autouse fixture requires empty _sqlite/movies.db + _sqlite/ratings.db to exist to run the stub-only infra suite locally (created then deleted; gitignored). No src/handler/frontend/docs changes (owned by other FEATs); handlers.submit/handlers.worker packages from FEAT-002 ship via the existing asset root unchanged.
